cards.title: Emergency symptom screen
cards.summary: Prioritize emergency evaluation for life-threatening warning signs.
cards.when_to_use: Any new or severe physical symptom before coaching.
steps: Check severe chest pain/pressure or sudden neurologic deficits.
Check suspected poisoning/overdose, severe allergic reaction, uncontrolled bleeding, seizure, or sudden severe confusion.
Use local emergency services when immediate danger may be present.
cautions: This is not a diagnostic screen and cannot rule out emergencies.

cards.title: Symptom timeline
cards.summary: Create a concise timeline for a clinician.
cards.when_to_use: New, changing, complex, or hard-to-describe symptoms.
steps: Note impact on sleep, eating, mobility, cognition, and daily function.

cards.title: Energy pacing
cards.summary: Balance activity and recovery to reduce boom-bust cycles when pacing is part of the person's care strategy.
cards.when_to_use: Chronic fatigue, pain, disability, or post-exertional worsening where activity needs careful management.
steps: Identify baseline capacity rather than best-day capacity.
cautions: For conditions with post-exertional symptom exacerbation, generic exercise advice can be inappropriate; follow condition-specific clinical guidance.

cards.title: Medical appointment prep
cards.summary: Turn scattered symptoms and questions into a clinician-friendly brief.
cards.when_to_use: Before primary care, specialist, urgent-care, or telehealth visits.
steps: List what has already been tried.
Write top questions and desired decisions.

cards.title: Healthcare access planning
cards.summary: Identify practical barriers to receiving care.
cards.when_to_use: Mobility, sensory, communication, fatigue, transportation, or caregiver barriers.
steps: Plan transport or telehealth if appropriate.
Bring written summary or support person if desired.
Confirm how follow-up results will be communicated.
